extracted.intended_audience: Users of pgf/TikZ creating inline graphics in TeX/LaTeX/ConTeXt/plain TeX (beginners and intermediate)
extracted.subtask_description: Creating inline graphics using the pgf system and the TikZ frontend: installation/load, choosing layers/frontends, constructing paths (lines, curves, circles, rectangles, grids), styling via options and styles, and seeking help/troubleshooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layered architecture: system/basic/frontend
rubrics_metrics.description: The pgf system consists of different layers: system layer, basic layer, and frontend layer. The system layer abstracts driver differences; the basic layer provides higher-level primitives; frontends (e.g., TikZ) provide easy-to-use syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a user you will not use the system layer directly. Use the frontend commands (TikZ) plus perhaps some basic-layer commands. Only use the system layer if you intend to write your own frontend or port pgf to a new driver. Example: system command \pgfsys@lineto{10pt}{10pt} vs. frontend \draw (0,0) -- (1,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer the TikZ frontend for everyday use
rubrics_metrics.description: The TikZ frontend is the 'natural' frontend for pgf: intended to be easy to use and gives access to all features of pgf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TikZ for concise metafont-like commands such as \draw (0,0) -- (1,0) -- (1,1) -- cycle; TikZ mixes ideas from metafont and pstricks but is not a full compatibility layer for either.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use system layer only for driver/porting tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The system layer is minimalistic and provides primitives mapping to backend driver commands; it is not intended for regular users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only interact with the system layer if you want to write a frontend or port pgf to a new driver. For ordinary drawings use the basic layer or a frontend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing between graphics packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider trade-offs between pgf/TikZ and alternatives (LaTeX {picture}, pstricks, xypic, dratex, metapost, xfig) when selecting a tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pgf/TikZ for portable inline programming and good label handling; pstricks is powerful but not portable to PDF engines; metapost is powerful but external and slower; xfig is WYSIWYG alternative. Pick the tool that fits portability, power, and workflow needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where drawing commands must live
rubrics_metrics.description: All TikZ graphic drawing commands must occur as an argument of \tikz or inside a {tikzpicture} environment; \draw is only defined inside these contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can write \begin{tikzpicture} ... \end{tikzpicture} (LaTeX), use \tikz{...} which collects up to the next semicolon, or engine-specific wrappers (plain TeX: \tikzpicture/\endtikzpicture, ConTeXt: \starttikzpicture/\stoptikzpicture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment/setup per TeX format
rubrics_metrics.description: Loading and environment commands differ by engine: LaTeX uses \usepackage{tikz}; plain TeX uses \input tikz.tex; ConTeXt uses \usemodule[tikz]; picture environment names differ accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using dvipdfm with plain TeX, set \def\pgfsysdriver{pgfsys-dvipdfm.def} before inputting tikz.tex or modify pgf.cfg. Use the appropriate wrapper commands for your TeX format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default coordinate units and reserved space
rubrics_metrics.description: In the initial coordinate system one unit equals 1cm. The tikzpicture environment automatically reserves enough space to encompass the picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of unit scaling when positioning elements; use transformations or explicit units when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paths as the basic building block
rubrics_metrics.description: A path is a series of straight lines and curves; construct paths by specifying a start coordinate (e.g., (0,0)) followed by path extension operations like --, .. controls .., circle, rectangle, grid, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example straight path: \draw (0,0) -- (1.5,0) -- (0,-1.5) -- (0,1.5); Paths are composed and then painted with commands such as \draw, \fill, \filldraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Straight path construction (--)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use -- to extend the current path in a straight line to another coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (-1.5,0) -- (1.5,0). You can concatenate many -- segments to form poly-lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curved path construction (Bézier controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use '.. controls (p1) and (p2) .. (end)' to add cubic Bézier curve segments. The first control point affects the tangent at the start; the second control point affects the tangent at the end. Omitting the second control reuses the first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (0,0) .. controls (1,1) and (2,1) .. (2,0); Use control points to shape tangents; understanding the tangent behavior is key to predictable curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circle and ellipse path operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'circle(radius)' to append a circle centered at the previous coordinate; use 'ellipse(xradius and yradius)' to append an ellipse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (0,0) circle (1cm); For rotated ellipses use transformations such as [rotate=30]. The previous coordinate is taken as the center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectangle path operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'rectangle' followed by a coordinate to append a rectangle where the previous and next coordinates are corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (0,0) rectangle (0.5,0.5); Handy for axis-aligned boxes; many rectangles can be drawn but special rectangle syntax is more convenient than composing from line segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grid path operation and steppings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'grid' path operation to add a grid that fills the rectangle from the current point to the following coordinate. Options include step=, xstep=, ystep=.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[step=.5cm] (-1.4,-1.4) grid (1.4,1.4); To subdue grid appearance set color and line width (e.g., [step=.5cm,gray,very thin]). Draw the grid first so other elements appear on top.

rubrics_metrics.name: Styles and style management
rubrics_metrics.description: Define reusable style names with \tikzstyle name=[options] or append with \tikzstyle name+=[options]. Styles can be based on other styles (style=...) and style names can be used directly as options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use styles to make code flexible and maintainable. Example: \tikzstyle help lines=[color=blue!50,very thin] then \draw[help lines] ... ; when adding options with += the new options override earlier ones where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options affecting drawing (color, draw, fill, line width, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Options influence how a path is drawn: color sets a general color, draw=color sets stroke color, fill=color sets interior fill color, line width controls stroke thickness, and many other graphic parameters exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use draw and fill separately when you need different stroke and fill colors. Examples in text: color=(color) vs. draw=(color) distinction; use options like very thin to control line width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformations for scaling/rotating
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ provides transformation options (scale, rotate, etc.) to change size and orientation of graphics; use them to scale everything or to rotate primitives like ellipses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \tikz \draw[rotate=30] (0,0) ellipse (6pt and 3pt); To enlarge an entire picture you can apply a global scale factor rather than changing every primitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: pgfpages for page management
rubrics_metrics.description: The subpackage pgfpages assembles several 'virtual pages' into a single physical page and can be used for n-up printing, watermarks, borders, and similar page-assembly tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pgfpages interrupts the shipout to store pages in a box and arranges them when enough virtual pages are collected. It can produce up to 16 pages per physical page and supports logos/watermarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting and where to get help
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended sequence when encountering problems: read the manual section relevant to your problem; check the SourceForge development page for reported issues; consult online forums and mailing lists; inspect the .log file before filing installation bug reports; as a last resort email the authors or mailing list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the .log file to ensure right files are loaded and avoid premature bug reports. Use the pgf/TikZ mailing list to increase chances of a response. Don't phone the author.
